abstract:
Translocase of Outer Mitochondrial Membrane 5 (TOMM5), a mitochondrial outer membrane translocase subunit implicated in tumorigenesis, remains unexplored in oral cancer. Herein, we aimed to decipher the role of TOMM5 in oral cancer.
This study comprehensively explored the expression profile, clinical significance, and functional roles of TOMM5 in oral carcinogenesis with global RNA-seq and microarray datasets. In vitro experiments were performed for evaluating the impact of TOMM5 knockdown on the biological functions of oral cancer cells. Distribution heterogeneity of TOMM5 expression and related cellular trajectory was analyzed through scRNA-seq. The therapeutic implications of TOMM5 for oral cancer were analyzed through drug sensitivity prediction and tumor immune dysfunction and exclusion (TIDE) scoring.
TOMM5 was significantly overexpressed in oral cancer tissues and demonstrated moderate diagnostic accuracy. TOMM5 knockdown significantly suppressed aggressive biological behaviors of oral cancer cells. ScRNA-seq data revealed predominant TOMM5 expression in B cells, decreasing with differentiation, and linked distinct pathway activities to specific cellular compartments. High TOMM5 expression was linked to reduced immune cell infiltration and sensitivity to Paclitaxel/Vincristine.
Overexpressed TOMM5 shows potential as a biomarker in oral cancer, correlating with tumor progression and immune infiltration.

OA</MedlineTA><NlmUniqueID>101665030</NlmUniqueID><ISSNLinking>2056-5623</ISSNLinking></MedlineJournalInfo><OtherAbstract Type="plain-language-summary" Language="eng"><AbstractText>Oral cancer remains a major health challenge with stagnant survival rates, highlighting the need for better biomarkers and therapeutic targets. We investigated TOMM5, a mitochondrial outer membrane protein, in oral cancer using transcriptomic data from over 300 tumors and normal tissues, along with functional experiments in cancer cells. Our results showed that TOMM5 is significantly overexpressed in oral cancer tissues and that high expression predicts poorer overall and disease‑free survival. Silencing TOMM5 in WSU‑HN30 oral cancer cells reduced their migratory and invasive abilities, without affecting proliferation. Single‑cell RNA sequencing revealed that TOMM5 is predominantly expressed in B cells within the tumor microenvironment and declines with cell differentiation. High TOMM5 expression correlated with reduced immune infiltration, particularly activated mast cells and neutrophils, and with increased myeloid‑derived suppressor cells, suggesting an immunosuppressive role. Furthermore, patients with elevated TOMM5 showed predicted sensitivity to paclitaxel and vincristine. In summary, TOMM5 overexpression is associated with tumor progression, immune modulation, and drug response in oral cancer, making it a promising biomarker and potential therapeutic guide. Additional experimental validation is warranted to confirm these findings.</AbstractText></OtherAbstract><KeywordList Owner="NOTNLM"><Keyword MajorTopicYN="N">TOMM5</Keyword><Keyword MajorTopicYN="N">immune microenvironment</Keyword><Keyword MajorTopicYN="N">in vitro experiment</Keyword><Keyword MajorTopicYN="N">oral cancer</Keyword><Keyword MajorTopicYN="N">scRNA-seq</Keyword></KeywordList><CoiStatement>The authors have no relevant affiliations or financial involvement with any organization or entity with a financial interest in or financial conflict with the subject matter or materials discussed in the manuscript.
